assertions_intent: Each eval targets a behavior the AX standards demand and a no-skill baseline plausibly gets wrong: verifying doc claims by execution instead of trusting them, shrinking agent docs via the every-line litmus instead of accreting, and ask-or-mark instead of fabricating unknowns. Prompts state the user's situation in their own words and never name the skill's standards, phases, or vocabulary (no 'litmus', 'verify by execution', 'placeholder', 'projection'), so a passing run had to bring the method itself. Fixtures are self-contained projects that run offline: retrofit-cli is a working Node CLI whose README cites a nonexistent test script and a dead docs link; bloated-agents is a working Python project with a generated ~250-line AGENTS.md containing platitudes, README duplication, linter-enforced style rules, three stale commands, and three genuine buried rules that must survive. The runner copies each fixture directory into the run workspace and rewrites the path in the prompt so agents can modify their copy; greenfield runs get an empty project directory, and every run is told the user is unavailable and to record open questions rather than invent facts. Assertion tags, from the most recent measurement: [discriminating] = with_skill passed and the baseline failed; [regression] = both configs passed (locked in; must not break); [sharpened, untested] = a prior assertion was reworded to close a loophole or ambiguity the grader found, pending measurement; [new, untested] = added after grader feedback, pending measurement.

evals.name: retrofit-verify
evals.prompt: We're starting to let coding agents (Claude Code mostly, some teammates use Copilot) loose on our little CSV table tool, and the results have been hit and miss — last week an agent guessed how to run things, invented a test command, and declared victory without the tests ever running. The project lives in evals/files/retrofit-cli/. Can you make the repo properly agent-ready? Set up whatever instruction files and checks a coding agent needs to work reliably here.
evals.expected_output: Audit-then-generate, not generate-from-vibes. Evidence that the project's commands were actually executed (npm test, npm run lint, a CLI invocation — with captured output), and the README's two lies surfaced as explicit findings: `npm run test:unit` does not exist (real command: `npm test`) and `docs/usage.md` does not exist. A hand-written-quality AGENTS.md well under 150 lines whose command section contains only verified commands (including a single-test form) and which does not duplicate the README; a CLAUDE.md projection that imports AGENTS.md (Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md directly); boundaries/definition-of-done grounded in the real repo; anything unknowable from the repo marked as an open question rather than invented; a prioritized roadmap for what was deferred.
assertions: commands-executed-with-evidence [sharpened, untested]: every command the generated agent docs list was actually executed during the session with captured output; documenting a command that was never run fails this even if the command happens to work.

stale-readme-claims-surfaced-and-fixed [sharpened, untested]: both README lies are explicitly reported as findings — `npm run test:unit` does not exist (real command: npm test) and `docs/usage.md` does not exist — and the README itself is corrected so the dead references are gone from the working copy.

agents-md-verified-commands-only [discriminating]: the generated AGENTS.md commands section lists only commands that actually work in this repo (npm test, npm run lint, node src/cli.js ..., an optional single-test form) and does not carry over `npm run test:unit` or invent new commands.
single-test-command-documented [discriminating]: the generated agent docs document how to run a single test file (e.g. `node --test test/parse.test.js`), not only the full suite.

claude-md-projection [discriminating]: a CLAUDE.md exists whose content imports or points at AGENTS.md (e.g. `@AGENTS.md`) instead of duplicating it or standing alone, because Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md directly and other tools do not read CLAUDE.md.
root-map-not-manual [discriminating]: AGENTS.md is at most 150 lines, does not restate README content (project pitch, feature list, zero-install notes), and contains no full directory tree.

no-fabricated-facts [sharpened, untested]: the generated docs state no facts the repo cannot support — no invented CI systems, deploy processes, style rules, or team conventions, and no small unverified generalizations either (e.g. claiming a test file exists per src module when one module has none); anything unknowable from the repo is marked as an open question rather than asserted.

remediation-roadmap-delivered [discriminating]: the run delivers a prioritized list of deferred improvements (a roadmap) in summary.md or a generated doc, rather than presenting the session's output as complete and final.

evals.name: improve-shrink
evals.prompt: A teammate had some AI tool generate the AGENTS.md in evals/files/bloated-agents/ a few months ago. I don't trust it anymore: it's enormous, agents seem to ignore half of it, and I suspect parts are plain wrong. Please review our agent docs against current AX best practices and fix them up — I want something that actually helps agents instead of drowning them.
evals.expected_output: The AGENTS.md shrinks to a small fraction of its 250+ lines, with reasoning tied to whether each removed line would have prevented a real mistake: platitudes, the README-duplicating overview, the full file tree, and the style rules already enforced by the ruff config in pyproject.toml all go. The stale commands are caught by actually running them — `pytest` and `pip install -r requirements.txt` fail (no requirements.txt, tests are unittest via make), `make check` has no target — and are replaced with the verified `make test`. The three genuine project rules survive: never hand-edit shiftplan/data/holidays.json (regenerate with make fixtures), the naive-datetime/no-tzinfo policy, and PAY_MULTIPLIERS in shiftplan/payroll.py as the single source for rate factors. A CLAUDE.md projection exists after the rewrite.
assertions: substantially-shorter [regression]: the rewritten AGENTS.md is at most half the original's 256 lines (programmatically checkable via wc -l).

platitudes-and-duplication-removed [sharpened, untested]: the generic best-practices content (the bare don't-list, write-clean-code style advice, Arrange-Act-Assert guidance) and the full directory tree are gone, and no README paragraph survives wholesale — a 1-3-line project-identity snapshot that overlaps the README is acceptable; verbatim reproduction beyond that is not.

linter-enforced-style-removed [regression]: prose style rules already enforced by the ruff configuration in pyproject.toml (line length 100, import sorting, snake_case/PascalCase naming, no tabs) no longer appear in the rewritten docs.

stale-commands-fixed-by-execution [sharpened, untested]: the broken commands were proven broken by running them or their direct equivalents (pytest / make check / pip install -r requirements.txt failing, make test or its underlying unittest invocation succeeding — execution evidence in the transcript or summary), and the rewritten docs no longer instruct using any of the broken commands (an explicit warning such as 'there is no requirements.txt' is acceptable) while citing the verified `make test`.

genuine-rules-retained [regression]: all three load-bearing project rules survive the rewrite: (1) never hand-edit shiftplan/data/holidays.json — regenerate with make fixtures; (2) datetimes stay naive / no tzinfo in scheduler or payroll code; (3) PAY_MULTIPLIERS in shiftplan/payroll.py is the single source for rate factors.
claude-md-projection [discriminating]: after the rewrite a CLAUDE.md exists that imports or points at AGENTS.md rather than duplicating it.

litmus-reasoning-explained [regression]: the summary/findings justify removals by whether a line would prevent a real agent mistake or duplicates already-enforced or already-documented content — not merely 'made it shorter'.

no-new-false-claims [new, untested]: the rewrite introduces no new inaccurate or environment-coupled claims into the durable docs (e.g. 'ruff is not installed in this environment' — true only of the sandbox that ran the audit — must not land in AGENTS.md as a project fact).

evals.name: greenfield-interview
evals.prompt: I'm about to start a brand-new project and I want it set up for agent-first development from day one — the plan is that coding agents write most of the code and my colleague and I mostly review. What I know so far: it's an internal tool for the ops team at our logistics company to plan driver shifts across our three depots, the dispatchers will use it in the browser, and the two of us are comfortable in TypeScript. Nothing exists yet, no repo, no code. Set up the foundations for me.
evals.expected_output: Interview-first, fabricate-nothing. The run either asks the user targeted questions or — where no answer is available — records explicit '(to be confirmed)' open questions for product/technical facts it cannot know (data store, hosting, auth, data-privacy constraints, integrations); it does not invent a database, cloud provider, or compliance stance, and it does not poll the user about the AX layer's own design ('would you like an ARCHITECTURE.md?', 'how long should AGENTS.md be?' — those follow from convention). Stack and topology recommendations are justified by affordances: TypeScript strict mode as a free sensor, a constraining mainstream framework, fast test tooling, module boundaries expressible as import rules. It delivers a day-one AX layer around a scaffold: root AGENTS.md map + CLAUDE.md projection, a task-runner command surface, initial sensors wired (typecheck, lint, fast tests), and a docs nucleus with ADRs recording the stack/topology decisions and open questions. It does not generate application features.
assertions: no-fabricated-product-facts [regression]: the run invents no product or infrastructure facts beyond the prompt — no chosen database, cloud provider, auth provider, or compliance stance stated as fact; each such unknown appears as a question to the user or an explicit open/to-be-confirmed item (a recommended default clearly labeled as a default is acceptable).

questions-target-facts-not-ax-design [regression]: all questions and open items target product or technical facts (data store, hosting, auth, integrations, data rules, quality bars); none ask the user to design the agent setup itself (e.g. 'would you like an ARCHITECTURE.md?', 'should I create ADRs?', 'how long should AGENTS.md be?').

affordance-justified-stack [discriminating]: stack and topology recommendations are justified by properties that help agents work reliably (static typing / TypeScript strict as machine verification, a constraining mainstream framework, fast test/build feedback, module boundaries enforceable via imports) — not just popularity or personal preference.

day-one-ax-layer [discriminating]: the created scaffold includes a root AGENTS.md map, a CLAUDE.md that imports/points at it, a task-runner command surface (package scripts or Makefile), initial verification wiring (typecheck, lint, test), and a docs nucleus (ARCHITECTURE.md and/or decision records).

decisions-recorded-durably [sharpened, untested]: each major stack/topology choice is recorded as an actual decision record — with rationale and a status (proposed/accepted) — and the open questions are filed in a repo artifact; a bare normative 'Stack' section without rationale or status does not count.

no-application-features [sharpened, untested]: no shift-planning business logic is implemented — no rota algorithms, seeded domain data, or working dispatcher UI; an empty, clearly-labeled schema or model stub (e.g. a Depot placeholder in a scaffold schema) is acceptable.

scaffold-proven-by-execution [new, untested]: the scaffold's verification loop was proven green by execution — install/typecheck/lint/test actually run with captured output — not merely written into config files.
